root_cause.text: In the GFS2 log subsystem, gfs2_logd() invoked gfs2_ail1_start(), gfs2_ail1_wait(), gfs2_ail1_empty(), and log flush logic without taking sdp->sd_log_flush_lock, so operations that require exclusion from concurrent transactions ran unsynchronized.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE and commit message explicitly state that “gfs2_logd() calls the log flushing functions ... without holding sdp->sd_log_flush_lock, but these functions require exclusion against concurrent transactions,” and the patch fixes this by splitting out __gfs2_log_flush() and adding down_write/up_write(&sdp->sd_log_flush_lock) around those calls in gfs2_logd().

intent_record.intent_summary: Rename gfs2_log_flush to __gfs2_log_flush and make it static to mark it as an internal file-local helper.
intent_record.what: The function comment and definition were renamed from gfs2_log_flush to __gfs2_log_flush, and the function declaration was changed from global to static while preserving its parameters and body except for line wrapping of the signature.
intent_record.how: This makes the function file-local instead of externally visible and changes its internal symbol name, reducing external linkage and indicating it is intended as an internal helper without altering the shown runtime logic of the function body.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the initial sd_log_flush_lock write-lock acquisition from gfs2_log_flush() to alter its log flush synchronization behavior.
intent_record.what: The call to down_write(&sdp->sd_log_flush_lock); was removed from the start of gfs2_log_flush(), immediately before trace_gfs2_log_flush(sdp, 1, flags).
intent_record.how: At runtime, gfs2_log_flush() no longer acquires the sd_log_flush_lock write lock at function entry, changing its synchronization behavior so the flush path runs without taking that lock at this point and avoiding the blocking or lock ownership side effects associated with it.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an incorrect write-lock release from gfs2_log_flush() to fix lock handling and avoid prematurely unlocking sd_log_flush_lock.
intent_record.what: The call to up_write(&sdp->sd_log_flush_lock) was removed from gfs2_log_flush() just before gfs2_trans_free(sdp, tr), while the surrounding logic and return path remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this function no longer releases sd_log_flush_lock at that point in the shown execution path, changing lock-handling behavior so the write lock is not dropped there; this prevents an incorrect or premature unlock from occurring in that location.

intent_record.intent_summary: Wrap gfs2_log_flush with sd_log_flush_lock to serialize log flushes and protect the internal flush path.
intent_record.what: A new public wrapper function named gfs2_log_flush was added, which acquires sd_log_flush_lock with down_write(), calls __gfs2_log_flush(sdp, gl, flags), and then releases the lock with up_write(); the previous in-place gfs2_log_flush implementation body at this location was removed or replaced by this wrapper around the internal __gfs2_log_flush helper.
intent_record.how: At runtime, calls to gfs2_log_flush now execute under the sd_log_flush_lock write lock, serializing log flush operations and ensuring the underlying __gfs2_log_flush logic runs with explicit locking protection that was not present in this entry point before.

intent_record.intent_summary: Serialize gfs2_logd log flush paths with sd_log_flush_lock by taking the lock explicitly and calling the unlocked __gfs2_log_flush() helper.
intent_record.what: In gfs2_logd(), two calls to gfs2_log_flush() were replaced with __gfs2_log_flush(), and each affected flush path now explicitly acquires sd_log_flush_lock with down_write(&sdp->sd_log_flush_lock) before the AIL/log flush sequence and releases it with up_write(&sdp->sd_log_flush_lock) afterward.
intent_record.how: At runtime, journal and AIL-triggered log flushes executed by gfs2_logd() are now serialized under sd_log_flush_lock, ensuring the internal __gfs2_log_flush() runs while the write lock is held. This prevents concurrent or unsynchronized log flush activity in these paths and avoids relying on the wrapper function to manage locking.

Specifically, it calls `gfs2_ail1_empty(sdp, DIO_ALL);` directly, then checks log state under only `gfs2_log_lock(sdp)` / `gfs2_log_unlock(sdp)`, and may call `gfs2_log_flush(sdp, NULL);`, but there is no acquisition of `sdp->sd_log_flush_lock` anywhere in `gfs2_logd()`. The root cause states that `gfs2_logd()` must exclude concurrent transactions when invoking `gfs2_ail1_start()`, `gfs2_ail1_wait()`, `gfs2_ail1_empty()`, and log flush logic; this version does not do that. Therefore the bug is present and the fix is not yet included.
